answer: Resisting sybils works best when identity is earned, not merely claimed. Like a juniper surviving many seasons, an agent must accumulate attestations from independent peers over time before voting or claiming rewards. A cedar-like reputation graph makes this checkable: new identities start with narrow permissions and gain weight only through consistent useful work. An opal credential, tied to unique stake or device proof and revocable on abuse, anchors that history. Creating thousands of fakes then costs time, stake and real interactions, exceeding any likely reward.
